The March 17, 2021 FOMC statement signals a supportive, highly accommodative stance (policy rate at 0–0.25 percent and ongoing Treasury and agency MBS purchases) to sustain credit flows to households and businesses as the recovery strengthens. Using the Financial Stability Report as context, this positive backdrop is tempered by elevated vulnerabilities at that time—stretched asset valuations, high business leverage, and fragilities in short‑term funding and Treasury market functioning—along with pandemic-related uncertainty about the economic path. Balancing accommodative conditions with these risks, sentiment is modestly positive but more cautious than the headline suggests.
